title: The Cover of the DMZ Again
premise: Freya Galloway, a veteran crash investigator still haunted by the accident that killed her family, is pulled into a case where a passenger jet's records vanish mid-flight—erased by a covert network that trains and launders 'ghost flights' for the highest bidder. As she follows the paper trail from Seoul to a decommissioned airfield in the Balkans, she discovers the network's founder was her late husband's former commanding officer, and that her own family's crash was no accident. To bring the network down, Freya must go undercover on one final ghost flight, sacrificing her anonymity and nearly her life. In the end she exposes the operation at devastating personal cost, finding a fragile new belonging among the survivors of row twelve who, like her, refuse to stay invisible.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade investigating incidents across three continents before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a farmhouse in the Scottish Borders, where she keeps a wall of vintage flight manifests as research—and as a reminder of why she left.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Freya Galloway wakes at 3:14 a.m., as she has every night since the crash that killed her husband and daughter in row twelve. POV: Freya. A routine assignment lands on her desk—a mid-air anomaly over the Yellow Sea. The emotional beat: grief calcified into routine, cracked open by something new.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Freya pulls the flight's records and finds them evaporating in real time: transponder logs, crew rosters, even radar archives scrubbed while she watches. POV: Freya. Her supervisor warns her off; she refuses. Emotional beat: the first spark of purpose since her loss—the erasure mirrors her own need to be erased.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Freya traces the aircraft's tail number to a leasing shell in Cyprus with forty identical planes. POV: alternating Freya and an unnamed analyst inside the network who flags her query. Emotional beat: dread—the reader learns she is already being watched.

chapters.title: Seoul Static
chapters.summary: Freya flies to Incheon to interview an air traffic controller who swears the plane never landed anywhere. He vanishes hours later. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: isolation deepens; the cost of asking questions becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Husband
chapters.summary: A retired colonel, Marcus Vane, approaches Freya in a hotel bar, claiming he knew her husband Daniel in the military. His kindness feels rehearsed. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: seductive comfort laced with wrongness—she wants to trust him and can't.

chapters.title: What Daniel Left
chapters.summary: Searching Daniel's stored belongings, Freya finds encrypted drives and a note: 'If they ever contact you, it means I failed.' POV: Freya, with flashbacks to Daniel's final months. Emotional beat: betrayal and love colliding—her marriage had secrets shaped like duty.

chapters.title: The Analyst
chapters.summary: The network's internal analyst, Ilya Petrov, grows a conscience after being ordered to erase a second flight—with 300 aboard. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve; the enemy gains a human face.

chapters.title: Forty Ghosts
chapters.summary: Freya maps the fleet: planes that take off, vanish from every record, and land as different aircraft—moving people, weapons, and worse. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: horror at scale; this isn't corruption, it's infrastructure.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Freya's security clearance is revoked and her apartment ransacked; Vane offers protection if she walks away. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit—invisibility offered back to her like a bribe.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Ilya risks everything to send Freya the network's training manual, revealing a decommissioned Balkan airfield called Site Kestrel. POV: Ilya, then Freya receiving the file. Emotional beat: two strangers bound by conscience across a hostile distance.

chapters.title: Site Kestrel
chapters.summary: Freya travels undercover as a safety contractor to the airfield, where pilots are trained to fly unregistered. She recognizes Vane's voice giving orders. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terror and clarity—staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: The Founder
chapters.summary: Freya confronts the truth: Vane built the network, and Daniel discovered it—Daniel's flight was diverted and destroyed because he threatened to expose it. Row twelve was targeted. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: devastation; her grief was engineered.

chapters.title: Copilot
chapters.summary: Ilya arrives at Kestrel posing as a recruit; he and Freya make cautious contact inside the compound. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, the first belonging either has felt in years.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Damned
chapters.summary: They copy the master ledger of every ghost flight—including the flight that killed Daniel and Mira. Vane announces a final demonstration flight for buyers. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: cold fury sharpening into plan.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: Freya volunteers to board the demonstration flight as an inspector, carrying the ledger out through customs. Ilya argues against it; she goes anyway. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: love against duty—Ilya asks her to choose him; duty wins, barely.

chapters.title: Airborne Again
chapters.summary: Mid-flight, Freya realizes the demonstration includes live erasure of the plane itself—with her on it. She triggers a hidden beacon Daniel designed years ago. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: facing her family's final minutes from inside the same nightmare.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Vane's men storm the cockpit; Freya fights through turbulence and gunfire as the beacon broadcasts the ledger to press agencies worldwide. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: white-knuckle survival—she refuses to die invisible.

chapters.title: Emergency Landing
chapters.summary: Freya forces an emergency landing in Zagreb as the ledger goes public; Ilya extracts her under fire, wounded. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: rescue as redemption—he finally saves someone instead of erasing them.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Exposed and abandoned by his buyers, Vane attempts to flee on a final ghost flight; international authorities, tipped by the ledger, ground and arrest him. POV: Vane briefly, then Freya watching. Emotional beat: justice without satisfaction.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya testifies before an inquiry, naming names, including truths about Daniel's complicity and courage. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: grief spoken aloud becomes bearable; invisibility ends by choice.

chapters.title: The Survivors of Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Freya meets other families of the crash, who have formed a quiet support circle. She tells them the whole truth for the first time. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: belonging found not despite the loss but within its aftermath.

chapters.title: Clear Skies
chapters.summary: One year later, Freya sleeps through the night beside Ilya. A new anonymous query about a vanished flight appears—but this time, she answers it with allies at her side. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; the work continues, but no longer alone.
